title: AI becomes a local-business discovery gateway, but consumer trust moves the decision into a cross-channel verification loop
geography: United States; consumers researching local businesses

observations.period: 2024-2026 annual Local Discovery Index editions; local-business discovery channels

denominator.unit: more than 1,000 U.S. consumers per 2026 survey; weighted by age, gender, and household income

ai_local_search_2026.unit: percent using an AI tool to find a local business in the last 30 days

ai_local_search_2025.unit: percent using AI search in the early-2025 comparison cited by SOCi

search_local_discovery.unit: percent using search for local discovery

social_local_discovery.unit: percent using social media for local discovery in 2026

multi_surface_discovery.value: Local discovery is becoming multi-surface rather than search-only: AI, search, social, maps, and reviews coexist in the same decision path.

observations.method: SOCi annual consumer survey, reported as the third edition of the Local Discovery Index; more than 1,000 U.S. consumers in 2026, weighted to mirror the U.S. population on age, gender, and household income; figures rounded.
observations.uncertainty: This is vendor-sponsored, self-reported consumer research; annual comparisons are not a panel, and survey wording, recruitment, and channel definitions limit causal or population-trend interpretation.
observations.subgroup: U.S. consumers by income, generation, local-business category, and discovery channel.
observations.counterinterpretation: Reported AI use may include embedded search summaries or broad AI-assisted research rather than a discrete replacement for search; industry marketing may emphasize adoption growth.

observations.period: 2026 Local Discovery Index; verification after an AI recommendation

denominator.unit: more than 1,000 U.S. consumers; AI-user and item-specific bases vary

wrong_local_business_information.unit: percent of AI users saying an AI tool gave them wrong information about a local business at least once

real_inconvenience.unit: percent reporting a real inconvenience from wrong local-business AI information

verify_before_contact.unit: percent taking a verification step before contacting a business after an AI recommendation

direct_contact_without_verification.unit: percent going straight from an AI recommendation to contacting the business

verification_loop.value: AI discovery does not end evaluation; inaccurate or incomplete answers push consumers into reviews, social media, independent search, or multiple-source checking before action.

observations.method: Self-reported survey of local-business discovery and post-recommendation verification behavior; SOCi reports the 2026 channel and trust estimates.
observations.uncertainty: The survey does not observe clickstream sequences, verify whether information was actually wrong, or identify whether verification improved purchase outcomes.
observations.subgroup: Consumers using AI for local-business discovery, with income and generational comparisons.
observations.counterinterpretation: Verification may be habitual rather than a response to distrust; respondents may overreport checking behavior.

observations.period: 2026 Local Discovery Index; reviews, responsiveness, and local conversion

denominator.unit: more than 1,000 U.S. consumers; item-specific bases vary

read_reviews.unit: percent reading reviews before a first visit at least some of the time

choose_business_responding_reviews.unit: percent more likely to choose a business that responds to reviews

helpful_response_revisit.unit: percent more likely to revisit after a helpful response to a negative review

negative_review_revise_after_response.unit: percent more likely to revise a negative review positively if the business responds helpfully

reputation_as_conversion_layer.value: Reviews and business responses function as a conversion and remedy layer between algorithmic visibility and local action, not merely as a ranking signal.

observations.method: Consumer survey estimates on review reading, business responsiveness, revisit intention, and review revision.
observations.uncertainty: Intentions and stated likelihood are not observed purchases, repeat visits, or review changes; the vendor's commercial position may shape emphasis on reputation management.
observations.subgroup: U.S. consumers by income, local-business category, and discovery pathway.
observations.counterinterpretation: People who value reviews may also be more conscientious evaluators and more likely to respond positively to any credible business information.

observations.period: 2026 Local Discovery Index; unequal adoption and category-specific discovery

denominator.unit: more than 1,000 U.S. consumers; subgroup bases vary

regular_ai_use_income_gap.value: Regular AI use rises from 47% among consumers earning under $50,000 to 76% among consumers earning $100,000 or more.

regular_ai_use_generation.value: Regular use is reported at 63% for Millennials, 49% for Gen Z, 48% for Gen X, and 11% for Baby Boomers.

category_path_difference.value: AI-first journeys are most common in healthcare and grocery, social is a notable starting point for financial services, and maps lead fuel and auto searches.

stratified_visibility.value: The AI-mediated local marketplace is not one uniform consumer shift: access, discovery route, and verification burden vary by income, generation, and category.

observations.method: SOCi subgroup and category analysis from the 2026 Local Discovery Index; descriptive comparisons are retained as reported rather than causal effects.
observations.uncertainty: Subgroup estimates may have larger uncertainty than the overall survey; category comparisons may reflect different search needs and respondent composition.
observations.subgroup: U.S. consumers by household income, generation, and local-business category.
observations.counterinterpretation: Observed differences may reflect age, income, device access, local business mix, or familiarity with AI rather than unequal platform power alone.

related_sources.claim: Official SOCi publication containing the 2026 Local Discovery Index findings, trend comparisons, methodology, channel use, verification behavior, review response, and subgroup estimates.

boundary: This record adds a local consumer-discovery route: AI increases discovery reach but shifts trust and conversion into a cross-channel verification loop involving search, reviews, social media, maps, and direct business information. It does not establish causal effects on sales, verify AI errors, observe individual journeys, or represent a probability sample; the research is vendor-sponsored and directional.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The official SOCi publication was reviewed for the Local Discovery Index sample description, annual comparison, AI and social discovery rates, incorrect-information and verification measures, review-response measures, income/generation differences, category variation, and limitations.
